issues.legal_issue: Small-plot sale transactions made after awareness of a proposed acquisition cannot establish the market value of a substantially larger tract without applying the prudent-purchaser test.
material_facts: A large tract was compulsorily acquired for a public purpose.
The reference court relied on several sales of small plots, including sales by the claimants, made after the sellers became aware of the proposed acquisition.
The reference court also relied on local rates used for stamp duty and assessed compensation on a square-foot basis.
The High Court accepted the reference court’s approach, subject to a deduction for development costs.
issues.conclusion: The lower courts applied a wrong principle by relying on the small-plot sales and fixing compensation on a square-foot basis without considering what a prudent purchaser would pay for the acquired tract in the open market.
issues.legal_principle: The court must assess reasonable compensation by sitting in the position of a prudent purchaser, avoiding speculation and asking whether such a purchaser would pay the proposed price in the open market. The landowner bears the burden of proving the prevailing market value. In compulsory acquisition, the court must provide fair compensation while avoiding an unnecessary burden on the public exchequer. The judgment refers to this as a settled principle of the Court but cites no earlier case by name; the acquisition proceeded under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

rule.if: compulsory_acquisition_compensation_appeal and large_tract_acquired and comparable_sales_involved_small_plots and (sales_followed_acquisition_awareness or sellers_were_claimants)

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_appe: The matter is an appeal concerning compensation for land taken by compulsory acquisition.
predicates.large_tract_acquired: A substantially large tract of land was acquired.
predicates.comparable_sales_involved_small_plots: The valuation relied on sales of plots substantially smaller than the acquired tract.
predicates.sales_followed_acquisition_awareness: The sales occurred after the sellers became aware of the proposed acquisition.
predicates.sellers_were_claimants: The claimants themselves made some of the sales relied on for valuation.
predicates.small_plot_sales_not_reliable_for_large_: The small-plot sales are not treated as reliable evidence of the market value of the acquired large tract.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns a large acquired tract and relies on small-plot sales made after acquisition awareness or by the claimants, those sales are not treated as reliable evidence of the tract’s value.

issues.legal_issue: An acquiring authority’s stated agreement to a market rate may be used to determine compensation when the court rejects the valuation approach adopted below.
material_facts: The acquiring authority stated in its case synopsis and through counsel that it was agreeable to a specified rate per acre.
The court rejected the lower courts’ method of valuing the acquired land by relying on the small-plot sales.
The court determined the market value at the rate to which the acquiring authority had agreed.
issues.conclusion: The market value was determined at the rate admitted by the acquiring authority.
issues.legal_principle: The court’s task is to assess reasonable market value using the prudent-purchaser test, and the landowner bears the burden of proving the prevailing market value. On the facts here, the acquiring authority’s stated agreement supplied the basis for determining the market value. The acquisition was under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; no earlier case is named in support of this valuation determination.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_appe: The matter is an appeal concerning compensation for land taken by compulsory acquisition.
predicates.acquiring_authority_admitted_market_rate: The acquiring authority stated that it was agreeable to a particular market rate.
predicates.lower_court_valuation_method_rejected: The court rejected the valuation method used by the lower court.
predicates.compensation_fixed_at_admitted_market_ra: The compensation is fixed using the market rate admitted by the acquiring authority.

issues.definition: If the acquiring authority admits a market rate in a compulsory-acquisition compensation appeal and the lower court’s valuation method is rejected, compensation is fixed at the admitted rate.

issues.legal_issue: An increase in compensation for compulsorily acquired land carries the applicable statutory solatium, interest, and additional amount.
material_facts: The court increased the compensation payable for the compulsorily acquired land.

The court stated that the claimants were entitled to solatium under Section 23(2), interest under Section 28 until deposit, and the additional amount under Section 23(1-A) on the enhanced compensation.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to the statutory solatium, interest, and additional amount on the enhanced compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 23(2), 28, and 23(1-A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 provide the applicable solatium, interest, and additional amount, respectively. The court applied those provisions to the enhanced compensation.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_awar: The proceeding concerns an award of compensation for land taken by compulsory acquisition.
predicates.compensation_enhanced: The court increases the compensation awarded for the acquired land.
predicates.claimant_entitled_to_statutory_additions: The claimant is entitled to the statutory additions applicable to the enhanced compensation.

issues.definition: When compensation in a compulsory-acquisition award is enhanced, the claimant is entitled to the applicable statutory additions.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s request for further enhancement is denied after the court determines compensation at the market rate supported by the acquiring authority’s admission.
material_facts: The claimant filed a cross-appeal seeking further enhancement of compensation.
The court determined the market value at the rate to which the acquiring authority had agreed.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s cross-appeal seeking further enhancement was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The court determined reasonable market value using the evidence before it and the acquiring authority’s stated agreement to a market rate; it then dismissed the claimant’s cross-appeal for further enhancement. The judgment cites no separate statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for dismissal.

predicates.claimant_cross_appeal_for_further_enhanc: The claimant files a cross-appeal seeking compensation beyond the amount otherwise determined.
predicates.market_value_fixed_at_admitted_rate: The court fixes the market value at a rate admitted by the acquiring authority.
predicates.further_enhancement_denied: The claimant’s request for further enhancement is dismissed.

issues.definition: If a claimant seeks further enhancement on cross-appeal after the court fixes market value at the acquiring authority’s admitted rate, further enhancement is denied.
